root_cause.text: The Intel uncore discovery parser failed to reject PCI devices from offline dies, so `uncore_discovery_pci()` could pass an out-of-range die index into `uncore_pci_pmu_register()` and overflow `pmu->boxes[]`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `die >= uncore_max_dies()` to the skip condition in `uncore_discovery_pci()` because “the discovery table continues to be parsed even if all CPUs in the associated die are offline,” which “can lead to an array overflow at `pmu->boxes[die] = box` in `uncore_pci_pmu_register()`.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an upper-bound validation for device die IDs before parsing the uncore discovery table.
intent_record.what: In uncore_discovery_pci(), the existing check `if (die < 0)` was expanded to `if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies()))`, so devices whose die ID is out of the valid range are now skipped as well.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now avoids passing an invalid die index to `parse_discovery_table()`. This prevents out-of-bounds access or misclassification when a device reports a die ID that is negative or greater than or equal to the maximum supported dies.

This passes the unchecked die value into the discovery parser path. Before the fix, there was no validation that the die index was within the online-die range, allowing propagation of an invalid index into PMU registration.
